graph.title: LEGO City 7992 Container Stacker
notes: Not a real problem: the booklet really builds separate models, so the graph keeps 6 unconnected groups on purpose. They are the red container (with its sticker sheet), the grey container, the gas-cylinder pallet, the two striped barrels, and the Container Stacker truck with its crane. Page 2 splits the parts into two bags: bag 1 builds the containers, pallet, barrels and minifigure; bag 2 builds the truck. The parts list and step pictures show no step that fastens one model to another. The cover shows them arranged as a display scene, which is not an assembly step, so no edges were invented between them.

Pieces are numbered in rough build order. Container and pallet pieces are b1-b47. The truck chassis and body are b48-b161. The crane is b162-b176. Axles and bushes are b177-b182. Barrels, hydraulic rods, wheels and goblets are in repeats.
The minifigure (hat, head, torso, legs) is not in the parts list, so it is not a node.

Many step pictures are ambiguous, so the exact piece-to-piece pairings are best guesses. The piece counts and types match the 214-piece list exactly, but adjacency was inferred. Examples are which of two similar plates a brick sits on, which side of the model a part goes on, and some assignments of grille tiles, 1x1 rounds, DBG 1x2 plates and green wedges.
The container side panels, columns and top plates are guessed. The red container uses 4 red panels and 2 columns; the grey container uses 2 grey panels and 2 columns.
Pieces whose exact stud or hole were not clear have null ports.
The wheel repeat has 6 copies. Copies 1-2 sit on the rear axle b177 and copies 3-6 on the front axle b180. Rod copy 2 attaches to pin b174 and pillar b74.
The sticker sheet b35 is a single node, given a contact edge to a red panel. Stickers are not modelled as separate parts.
The radio and wrench are attached to the two clip plates on the cab platform. Which goes in which clip is assumed.
The chassis may be shown flipped in some steps (pages 15-19), so top and bottom assignments of the red and yellow plates are uncertain.
